messages.subject: MLM and ML estimator
parts:
Hi Everyone,
I'm new in SEM and lavaan. I'm estimating a model with Satorra-Bentler and robust standard errors but there is something I didn't know.
when I set estimator="MLM", the output is

lavaan (0.5-16) converged normally after  31 iterations

  Number of observations                            30

  Estimator                                         ML      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               56.362      54.279
  Degrees of freedom                                33          33
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.007       0.011
  Scaling correction factor                                  1.038
    for the Satorra-Bentler correction

but in the same model when i just using ML method, the oupput is

lavaan (0.5-16) converged normally after  31 iterations

  Number of observations                            30

  Estimator                                         ML
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               44.513
  Degrees of freedom                                24
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.007

why ML and MLM give different degree of freedom and the value of its minimum function test statistic also?can anyone explain me about it, please?

thanks a lot for your time.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: MLM and ML estimator
parts: why ML and MLM give different degree of freedom and the value of its minimum function test statistic also?can anyone explain me about it, please?

It's hard to say anything about your model without any information about your model (i.e., syntax).  When I've seen DF change like this in the past, it has been because one call to lavaan was made with "fixed.x = TRUE" and another was made with "fixed.x = FALSE", perhaps inadvertently when specifying one option changed the default setting for fixed.x (although I don't think estimator = "MLM" or se = "robust" would change fixed.x from TRUE to FALSE).  Regardless, seeing your syntax (and perhaps data) would be more revealing.

Terry
